bypass.note: Saudi Abqaiq→Yanbu, 5 mb/d capacity (EIA). Barrels then load at Yanbu on the Red Sea, where they are exposed to Bab el-Mandeb risk.
UAE Habshan→Fujairah, ~1.5–1.8 mb/d capacity, loads outside the strait.
Iraq→Turkey, ~1.6 mb/d nameplate. Restarted 18 Mar 2026 at ~250 kb/d; usable volume depends on Baghdad–Erbil–Ankara politics. Not counted.

strait-of-hormuz.bypass_note: EIA estimates ~2.6 mb/d of spare Saudi (East-West, 5 mb/d) and UAE (Habshan–Fujairah, 1.8 mb/d) pipeline capacity could bypass Hormuz; the split shown is approximate. Iran's Goreh–Jask line adds ~0.3 mb/d. Kuwait, Qatar, Bahrain and Iraq's Basra exports and all Gulf LNG (~one-fifth of global LNG trade) have no bypass. 84% of Hormuz crude and 83% of its LNG went to Asia in 2024.

exposed.note: Top destination for Hormuz crude. China, India, Japan and South Korea together took 69% of Hormuz crude and condensate in 2024 (EIA).
~half of crude imports and most LPG/LNG imports come from the Gulf.
~90%+ of crude imports from the Middle East.
~70% of crude imports from the Middle East; major Qatari LNG buyer.
Qatari LNG and Middle East diesel/jet fuel; indirect exposure through global prices.

bab-el-mandeb.bypass_note: 1H 2025 flows (EIA), already reduced by Houthi attacks; ~8.7 mb/d moved through before them (1H 2023). No pipeline bypass: traffic reroutes around the Cape of Good Hope. Yanbu cargoes heading north to Europe can still reach Suez/SUMED without crossing the strait.

exposed.note: Middle East crude, diesel and jet fuel via Suez; longer voyages raise delivered costs.
Suez Canal and SUMED revenues collapse when traffic diverts.
Yanbu exports (the Hormuz bypass outlet) sit inside the Red Sea.

strait-of-malacca.bypass_note: Ships can divert via the Lombok/Makassar or Sunda straits at the cost of ~2–3 extra days. China's overland pipelines (Central Asia, Russia, Myanmar) cover only a small share of its imports. Baseline: EIA 1H 2025 flows.

exposed.note: ~80% of oil imports ("Malacca Dilemma").
Nearly all Gulf crude and LNG passes Malacca or nearby straits.
Same exposure as Japan.
Almost entirely dependent on seaborne energy imports.

panama-canal.bypass_note: US Gulf LNG to Asia diverts via the Cape of Good Hope or Cape Horn, adding ~2 weeks. That ties up LNG carrier capacity and raises Asian spot prices. Oil figure is approximate. Baseline: EIA 1H 2025 flows.

exposed.note: US LNG and LPG cargoes to Northeast Asia.
Longer voyages make Asian sales less competitive; more cargoes default to Europe.
